cohort: 200 patients undergoing cesarean section at Shadan Institute of Medical Sciences Hyderabad between October 2017 and September 2019, with 100 in each exposure group (emergency vs elective).
finding: Emergency cesarean section was associated with significantly more maternal (haemorrhage, uterine incision extension, blood transfusion, postpartum haemorrhage) and fetal (meconium-stained liquor, NICU admission) complications compared to elective cesarean section.
